header.name: Modeling and Analysis of Random 5G Networks
header.description: This course will commence with introduction to the tools from stochastic geometry, applied in the context of wireless network modeling. Then, the course will build up on the learned tools to model several features of 5G systems such as mm-wave communication, massive MIMO, ultra dense networks etc. Detailed PHY layer aspects will be translated into simplistic stochastic geometry models, for performing system-level analysis. A notion of performance metrics for the users in modern wireless systems will be developed, e.g., SINR coverage, rate coverage, positioning accuracy, network load etc. The fundamental tractability-accuracy tradeoffs will be discussed while choosing appropriate stochastic geometry tools for modeling 5G networks. Impact of physical layer modeling on the MAC layer protocols will be studied and accordingly, cross-layer algorithms will be discussed. Throughout the course, several real-world examples will be demonstrated showcasing the practical impact of the tools learned in the course.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to characterize 5G cellular and ad-hoc systems in terms of their QoS requirements and enabling technologies.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply mathematical results of stochastic geometry to model and analyze 5G wireless systems. Additionally, they will be able to extract system parameters for different models from 3GPP specifications.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The students will be able to perform system level analysis of mm-wave cellular networks.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: The students will be able to perform deployment planning and network dimensioning for a cellular operator intending to deploy 5G systems for heterogeneous service requirements.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: The students will be able to derive fundamental results of classical point processes, e.g., nearest neighbor distance, PGF, MGF, etc. Additionally, for any novel point process assmed in their model in the project work, the students should be able to derive the same metrics.
